entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack

sentences.text: 06 . (Through hybrid mode) 1

This is an application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with Balasore Sadar P.S. Case No.245 of 2023 corresponding to C.T. Case No.483 of 2023, pending in the file of the learned J.M.F.C.(City), Balasore under Sections 403, 409, 420 of IPC.
2. The prayer of the petitioner has been rejected vide order dated 12.09.2023 by the learned Addl.
Sessions Judge -cum- P.O., Designated Court under OPID Act, Balasore.

3. The allegation against the petitioner is that the petitioner was working as Section Commercial Officer in Sargaon Section under Balasore Electrical Circle of TPNODL, Balasore since December,
2021.

entities.text: Balasore Electrical Circle of TPNODL, Balasore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On 23.08.2023, the office received written complaint from the consumers stating that they had made payment to the petitioner but receipt was not provided.
Subsequently, other complaints were received that receipts issued by the petitioner did not match with TPNODL financial records.
The other allegation against the petitioner are that he did not deposit Rs.9.98 lakhs which had ben collected by him from the consumers.
On the basis of this information, it was ascertained that Rs.15 lakhs loss had been caused to the company and trust of the consumer had been eroded by this activity.

4. Mr. K.K. Jena, learned counsel for the petitioner had submitted that the petitioner has already refunded Rs.1,85,000/- and is prepared to deposit Rs.2,00,000/- initially and will deposit a further Rs.1,00,000/- within one month after he is released on bail and refund the entire amount if he is allowed to continue in his job.
He had filed an affidavit of the father of the petitioner to that effect.

entities.text: Arun Kumar Jena vs State Of Odisha

sentences.text: Mr. K.K. Jena, learned counsel for the petitioner produces a demand draft No.881780 dated 16.11.2023 drawn on the State Bank of India, Kaipada SAB for a amount of Rs. 1,98,000/- drawn in favour of T.P. Northern Odisha Distribution Ltd.

entities.text: State Bank of India, Kaipada SAB
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He submits that as per undertaking given to this Court on 15.11.2023, this draft has been prepared.

5. Mr. L. Mishra, learned counsel for the informant submits that the draft may be submitted in the Court of learned S.D.J.M., Balasore as he has no instructions to accept the demand draft on behalf of the informant.
Hence the demand draft is returned to the learned counsel for the petitioner.
He has filed a memo alongwith a Photostat copy of the demand draft which is taken on record.

6. Mr. L. Mishra, learned counsel for the informant files a memo along with the clarification dated 16.11.2023 issued by the SEEC, Balasore to Sub-Inspector, Sadar Police Station, Balasore in relation to letter dated 09.11.2023 issued by the Executive Engineer (Elect), C.E.D., Balasore with regard to information sought by the I.O. vide letter dated 31.10.2023 where it is stated that (1) the amount misappropriated through mobile App during January to August, 2023 is Rs.1,98,313/-and (2) The amount misappropriated from customer during January to August, 2023 is Rs.6,35,794/-.
The total comes to Rs.8,34,107/-.
He has requested to ignore the previous communication.
The letter is taken on record.

7. Mr. Mishra submits that as per the affidavit dated 12.10.2023 the informant has stated in paragraph-10 that a sum of Rs.6,35,794/- has already been returned to the consumers by TPNODL and they were anticipating receipt of new complaints from the consumers in the next 2-3 billing cycles and Rs.1,98, 313/- is the additional affidavit.
8.

Considering the submissions of the learned counsels, the nature of allegations against the petitioner, the prevaricating statements of the informant and the affidavit filed on behalf of the petitioner, production of demand draft for Rs.1.98 lakhs and the period of his detention in judicial custody I am inclined to allow the prayer for bail.
9.

Let the petitioner- Arun Kumar Jena be released on bail on such terms and conditions as may be fixed by the learned Court below in seisin over the matter, subject to his depositing an amount of Rs.3,50,000/- in the learned Court below, including the following conditions:
(i) He will not indulge in any criminal activity while on bail.
(ii) He will not threaten or try to influence prosecution witnesses while on bail.
(iii) He shall report before the IIC, Balasore Sadar Police Station on every Sunday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. till conclusion of trial.
(iv) He will remain present in the trial Court on each date it if fixed for trial unless his appearance is dispensed with by the learned trial Court under Section 317 Cr.P.C. on any particular day.

Arun Kumar Jena vs State Of Odisha ..... Opp. Party on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190748101/
2 (v) He shall pay the balance amount which is legally due from him in installments within a period of six months.
10. Violation of any condition will entail in cancellation of bail.

12. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application.
13.
